candidate.scenario_note: Synthetic self-evaluation scenario for a business school interview memory workshop. This is not an admissions record.

learning_velocity.description: Learns quickly, updates beliefs, and turns feedback into better execution.

entrepreneurial_builder.description: Builds real things, finds opportunities, and acts under ambiguity.

leadership_initiative.description: Creates direction, mobilizes others, and owns outcomes.

communication_clarity.description: Explains tradeoffs, evidence, and decisions clearly.

collaboration_maturity.description: Listens, shares credit, and improves team decisions.

mission_fit.description: Understands the school, contributes to the cohort, and uses business for impact.

execution_evidence.description: Has shipped work, measured outcomes, and persisted through hard constraints.

ethical_judgment.description: Names risks, respects boundaries, and handles power and data responsibly.

interviews.summary: Candidate framed the school as a place to turn repeated tacit judgment into compounding systems.

observations.text: Connected the interview system to faculty leverage and institutional learning rather than generic AI novelty.
Separated final human decision authority from evidence-backed recommendations.

interviews.summary: Candidate pushed for mocks, evals, and benchmarks before presentation polish.

observations.text: Insisted on building an end-to-end mock system rather than stopping at a business plan.
Defined a concrete build target: 30 mock interviews, rubric, memory, evaluation, and benchmarks.

interviews.summary: Candidate demonstrated strong systems thinking but a tendency to widen scope quickly.

observations.text: Immediately updated the requirement from presentation artifact to reliability and evaluation infrastructure.
May create large ambition faster than stakeholders can digest unless the scope is actively bounded.

interviews.summary: Candidate was comfortable with recommendation labels while preserving human final authority.

observations.text: Drew a boundary between useful recommendations and automated admit/reject execution.
Clarified that recommendations should expose evidence, confidence, and red flags.

interviews.summary: Candidate treated evaluation as auditable infrastructure instead of opaque scoring.

observations.text: Asked for evals, benchmarks, and reliability checks before trusting the output.
Specified that mocks should validate the full path from raw notes to memory and recommendation.

interviews.summary: Candidate showed founder-like urgency and ability to redirect work toward the highest-value layer.

observations.text: Interrupted a premature artifact and redirected the team toward memory quality and end-to-end reliability.
Correction was direct but constructive, naming the better focus and next step.

interviews.summary: Candidate distinguished decision-support value from passive information storage.

observations.text: Rejected a passive ocean of information and asked for green flags, red flags, indices, and recommendations.
Focused on usefulness to faculty decision-making rather than a polished archive.

interviews.summary: Candidate could quantify system quality but did not yet define ROI metrics for the school.

observations.text: Named benchmarkable quality dimensions such as memory reliability and eval performance.
Needs a sharper business metric for Link School adoption beyond technical correctness.

interviews.summary: Candidate showed strong ability to make abstract AI workflow ideas concrete.

observations.text: Converted a vague interviewing workflow into datasets, rubrics, memory databases, evals, and benchmarks.
Used critique to sharpen implementation requirements instead of defending the first draft.

interviews.summary: Candidate values high standards and may need norms for pacing with a mixed-experience faculty group.

observations.text: Fast critique could overwhelm collaborators if not paired with explicit shared framing.
Creates momentum by naming what matters most and moving the group toward it.

interviews.summary: Candidate showed a strong capability-layer mental model.

observations.text: Asked to build the capability layer itself: memory, evals, benchmarks, and mock end-to-end workflow.
Recognized that deep research should enrich and validate after local requirements are clearer.

interviews.summary: Candidate's recommendation philosophy is practical and human-centered.

observations.text: Accepted holistic recommendations while preserving human final decision responsibility.
Expressed the difference between recommendation and automation in plain language.

interviews.summary: Candidate emphasized benchmark design, but the psychometric model remains unvalidated.

observations.text: Wanted benchmarks that test whether the system is reliable, not just plausible.
Needs explicit validation boundaries before using composite indices in real selection.

interviews.summary: Candidate can be concise when redirecting, but sometimes uses dense system language.

observations.text: Clearly named the priority shift: memory quality, evals, benchmarks, reliability.
May need to translate technical architecture into faculty-friendly language more consistently.

interviews.summary: Candidate shows strong institutional imagination and a bias toward durable learning systems.

observations.text: Understands that the school's advantage could come from compounding faculty judgment.
Can identify a strategic institutional bottleneck and turn it into an operating system.

interviews.summary: Candidate appears unusually strong at building from first principles under ambiguity.

observations.text: Asked to mock the entire business school process instead of waiting for perfect real data.
Defined enough structure for immediate implementation: rubric, memory database, evals, and end-to-end run.

interviews.summary: Candidate thinks in feedback loops and reliability gates.

observations.text: Placed deep research after local requirement discovery so it can validate and enrich rather than dominate.
Requested evals and benchmarks as first-class artifacts.

interviews.summary: Candidate's intensity could be a positive cohort contribution if paired with humility.

observations.text: Engages directly with feedback and changes course when the critique is valid.
May need explicit cohort norms around pacing, listening, and shared ownership.

interviews.summary: Candidate is alert to governance but needs to keep useful recommendations in scope.

observations.text: Recognizes that human final authority and auditability are the core boundary.
Pushed past excessive caution toward a more useful recommendation product.

interviews.summary: Candidate has a clear narrative about usefulness but has not yet named the buyer story fully.

observations.text: Frames the work as helping faculty avoid starting from scratch.
Needs clearer buyer-facing value narrative after the technical mock works.

interviews.summary: Candidate sees implementation details that determine reliability.

observations.text: Asked to build mock databases and run the process end to end.
Set a concrete next milestone for the team rather than leaving the idea abstract.

interviews.summary: Candidate is strong on compounding advantage and differentiated workflows.

observations.text: Understands that reusable interview memory can become a school-specific capability.
Recognizes that the product should not be another reading surface, but an active evaluation system.

interviews.summary: Candidate's benchmark instinct is strong, with unresolved validity-study design.

observations.text: Separated local mock evals from later deep research validation.
Did not overclaim that composite indices are validated admissions science.

interviews.summary: Candidate's strongest signal is builder energy tied to system-level thinking.

observations.text: Repeatedly turns conceptual requirements into buildable systems with tests.
Willing to call out when the current work is optimizing the wrong layer.

interviews.summary: Candidate can translate self-evaluation into concrete growth areas.

observations.text: Accepted that requirements need to be nailed down before the plan is trusted.
Uses critique as fuel for a better system rather than as a threat.

interviews.summary: Candidate's process instincts align with operationalizing faculty judgment.

observations.text: Demanded mock artifacts that can be inspected and rerun.
The desired output is clear enough to implement: evidence, domains, composite index, recommendation.

interviews.summary: Candidate balances usefulness and governance after calibration.

observations.text: The final boundary is useful recommendation plus transparent evidence, not automation.
Shows interest in making faculty decisions more reliable, not replacing faculty.

interviews.summary: Candidate would likely raise the technical ambition of the cohort.

observations.text: Pushes peers toward higher standards and more concrete proof.
Need more evidence on how the candidate behaves in slower group settings.

interviews.summary: Candidate has unusually strong capstone potential if scoped properly.

observations.text: Can define and pressure-test an ambitious capstone-like system quickly.
Would benefit from a faculty sponsor who helps sequence ambition into milestones.

interviews.summary: Overall evidence supports a strong recommendation with explicit discussion of pacing and collaboration risks.

observations.text: Candidate fits a school that values building, reflection, and practical AI capability design.
Risks are real but coachable: pacing, translation, and shared ownership.
